Maria (runtime): Quick thread — ran the long-context profiler on the chat workload. Prefill accounts for ~68% of p99 tail when context >1k. Proposal: switch to phase-based accounting and apply different microbatch caps per phase. Thoughts? :thinking:

Devin (infra): Can you share perf numbers + which kernels were used? My worry: if we reduce prefill batch size we might lose throughput because some kernels need larger batches to stay efficient.

Maria (runtime): Profiler summary:
```
workload: chat-long
samples: 12k
prefill: p50=42ms p95=95ms p99=320ms (~68% of p99)
decode: p50=12ms p95=36ms p99=110ms (~24% of p99)
other (scheduling/kvcache): ~8%
microbatch histogram: median 4, mean 6, tail 32
```
Main takeaway: prefill tail is dominant for long-context requests (lots of KV activity + kernel path change).

Arun (mlperf): Two suggestions: a) dynamic microbatch caps keyed by sequence-length histogram so long-context requests don't hog large prefill batches; b) kernel hysteresis — only switch kernels if expected throughput/latency delta exceeds a threshold (e.g., >5% throughput or >10% latency improvement) to avoid oscillation.

Sophia (eng-sre): Agree on hysteresis. Also saw KV cache miss spikes aligning with prefill tails in last incident — pre-warming common prefixes could shave p99.

Maria (runtime): Here's an example queuing trace from the run (trimmed). You can see a microburst of mobile requests causing microbatch size to jump then KV miss storms. I'm thinking phase-SLO mapping: prefill p95 target = 80ms, decode p95 target = 40ms, and allocate headroom for scheduling jitter.

Devin (infra): Cool. What quantiles did you compute for the reporting? p50/p95/p99 all present?

Maria (runtime): Yes — we measured p50/p95/p99. Reposting the key numbers above. On our a2-small-ish nodes these numbers hold; results will differ on A100-backed fleets but relative split persists.

Devin (infra): ACK. I'll run a scheduler sweep sim with phase-based caps. If prefill dominates p99 we should prioritize kernel specialization for the long-context prefill path and KV prefetch heuristics.

Arun (mlperf): Also consider separate KV cache tiers or TTL per phase — prefix cache hotness should be preserved for decode while allowing aggressive eviction for bulk prefill state to avoid thrashing.

Sophia (eng-sre): From an ops perspective: rollout plan should be a canary that enables phase-based microbatch caps + KV pre-warm for ~1% traffic, with metric gates: phase_latency_p95, phase_latency_p99, kv_miss_rate, end-to-end error rate.

Maria (runtime): I'll draft an RFC with simulation results and a canary checklist. Volunteers to co-author? @Arun (mlperf) @Devin (infra)

Devin (infra): I'll co-author. Drop the raw traces in perf-bucket and I'll run the kernel-selection sims.
